name: Corporate statism
summary: Corporate statism organises society into officially designated functional groups, usually by economic sector, that the state recognises, controls and incorporates into policymaking. It replaces class conflict and party competition with state-arbitrated cooperation among employers, workers and other interests, within a strong, authoritarian state. Private ownership usually survives, under heavy state direction of investment, wages and prices.
scope: The authoritarian state-corporatist strand as practised in Mussolini's Italy (1922-1943), Salazar's Estado Novo in Portugal, and the interwar Austrian Federal State, with Othmar Spann's theory and Catholic social teaching (Quadragesimo Anno) as intellectual sources. It excludes democratic neo-corporatism or social partnership and corporate nationalism, which works through private corporations. Many non-economic questions are inferred from the regimes' Catholic-traditionalist and nationalist character, and Fascist Italy differed from Portugal on war, race and the leader cult.

keyFigures.name: Benito Mussolini
keyFigures.role: Leader of Fascist Italy, whose corporate state is the best-known example

keyFigures.name: António de Oliveira Salazar
keyFigures.role: Architect of Portugal's corporatist 1933 constitution and ruler of the Estado Novo

keyFigures.name: Othmar Spann
keyFigures.role: Austrian theorist whose universalist ideas are linked to corporate statism

sources.usedFor: 1933 constitution, state syndicates, one party, anti-parliamentarism, mixed protectionist economy, empire, family motto

universal-healthcare.rationale: Estado Novo and Italy added state-run social insurance as the price of syndicate membership, but universal tax-funded care was not a doctrinal aim; inferred from the welfare-for-legitimacy bargain.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages were set by state-supervised collective contracts between recognised bodies, not by a statutory floor, and adherents leaned towards restraint rather than substantial rises.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Corporatists hold that free competition cannot direct economic life and must be coordinated by state-recognised bodies, though private enterprise is retained.

public-ownership.rationale: The Estado Novo kept a mixed economy with private ownership under heavy state regulation, so wholesale public ownership was not the model.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Corporate statist regimes harnessed capitalists as partners and did not campaign on soaking the rich; no clear doctrine, so split.

unions-good.rationale: Free unions were replaced by state-controlled official syndicates, so independent unions are rejected even though state-run syndicates are central.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property is kept, but with a social function and state limits for the common good, so adherents neither treat it as inviolable nor reject it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The state has broad authority over investment, wages and prices, and economic actors are subordinated to the national interest.

cut-welfare.rationale: Regimes offered welfare to syndicalised workers to win loyalty; cutting it runs against the bargain, though welfare was not expansive.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers are organised into syndicates beside employers rather than owning firms; Quadragesimo Anno advises that workers may share in ownership, management or profits through partnership contracts, but not collective ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred and anachronistic: the Estado Novo's political police PIDE investigated and persecuted opponents, suggesting security was put above liberty.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the conservative, order-oriented moral stance of Catholic-authoritarian corporate regimes.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addressed; these regimes restricted speech widely but for political reasons, not on hate-speech grounds.

strong-leader.rationale: The Estado Novo article says the president was on paper a virtual dictator and that his power to dismiss Salazar was the only check on Salazar's power under an anti-parliamentarian constitution.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is the organising centre of society; the Fascist formula was everything within the state, nothing outside it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; authoritarian states generally monopolise force and restrict private arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order-based regimes emerging from the 1926 coup relied on police and military backing and suppressed opposition.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic, family-centred moral order of the Estado Novo and Fascist Italy.

decide-locally.rationale: Corporate statism is centralised, with sectoral bodies recognised and controlled by the national state.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not central to the doctrine; regimes mixed harsh repression with rhetoric of order.

traditional-family.rationale: The Estado Novo motto was God, Fatherland and Family, and labour associations were framed as natural orders like the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic traditionalism of the family-centred regimes.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholic-influenced and pronatalist regimes opposed abortion; inferred from the Estado Novo's Catholic social doctrine.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Estado Novo drew on Catholic social doctrine, with the Church privileged, though Fascist Italy was more ambivalent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; the regimes were nationalist and colonial and did not pursue such redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family ideal and the regimes' conservative gender order.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nation-first traditionalism, as in God, Fatherland and Family, makes cultural preservation central.

gradual-change.rationale: The regimes broke with liberal parliamentary institutions yet claimed to preserve a natural social order; adherents are split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and the corporatist focus on organised national producers; not a documented priority.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalist regimes put sovereignty first; inferred, not a doctrinal topic.

free-trade.rationale: The Estado Novo ran strong protectionism and corporatist regimes favoured managed national economies.

nation-first.rationale: Nation-centred, with Portugal's pluricontinental nation and Italian nationalism as pillars.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the sovereignty-first nationalism of these regimes.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss borders, but a nation organised into state-defined bodies is hard to square with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Corporate states pursued national production and development; degrowth is an anachronism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the state could direct action but the ideology has no environmental stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented doctrine on technological progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a state-directed development outlook.

revolution-justified.rationale: Corporatists present themselves as ending class conflict and preserving order, rejecting revolution from below, though Fascism came to power by force.

experts-over-public.rationale: Policy is made through designated functional bodies and the state rather than mass electoral politics.

central-planning.rationale: These regimes directed investment and wages but kept private ownership, not comprehensive central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ownership by workers or the public is not the corporatist model of private owners and workers cooperating under the state.

land-value-tax.rationale: Corporate statism has no documented position on land taxation, and nothing in its principles points either way.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the retention and defence of private property and family continuity.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare was tied to syndicate membership and work, not unconditional.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Estado Novo was strongly protectionist and corporate states favoured managed national economies.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Estado Novo article states that the state exercised extensive authority over private investment decisions and the level of wages.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno favours wide ownership but the regimes protected large business too; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno rejects the view that the wage contract is unjust in itself and demands a wage sufficient to support a worker and his family.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Strong state economic control is inconsistent with abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The defining feature: citizens organised into state-recognised bodies, with the state as final arbiter of wages and conditions.

one-party-rule.rationale: Italy and Portugal ran single-party states, though corporate statism is more about a ruling party mediating; the Estado Novo party was a support structure and not ideologically driven.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Regimes varied (Italy kept a king, Portugal a republic, Austria Catholic authoritarian); no uniform stance.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1933 constitution set up an anti-parliamentarian and authoritarian government and restricted the legislature to members of the National Union.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscites were used for legitimacy as in 1933, but direct legislative votes were not a principle.

workers-councils.rationale: Official workers' syndicates replaced free trade unions and sat in a state corporative chamber, so independent workers' councils as the basis of power are implied to be rejected.

right-to-secede.rationale: Portugal treated its colonies as extensions of the nation and centralised states reject secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hierarchical order and strong leadership mean adherents accept that some are suited to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Regimes used violence and a secret police against opponents and claimed rule by force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Stronger for Fascist Italy than Salazar's Portugal, which stayed neutral, so mixed and inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The regimes allied with the Church and Catholic social doctrine, not strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic natural-law inspiration is influential but laws were not framed on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Corporate statism makes the state the organising centre of society, so handing courts, policing and defense to private firms contradicts its premise.

military-superiority.rationale: Strong state power and nationalism lead to a preference for strength, though small Portugal was less ambitious.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Italy and Portugal's corporatism is not primarily ethnic; Austrian and Italian versions differ.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno asks the State to end conflict between hostile classes and the Fascist Labour Charter was a form of class collaboration; the historical thesis itself is not discussed.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno criticises the huge gap between rich and propertyless, but the system keeps owners and wage earners in distinct, harmonised orders rather than seeking equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; colonial states denied such authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Regimes defended their empires as civilising projects.

civilizational-union.rationale: Corporate statism is a mode of social organisation within a state and is silent on civilizational blocs; regimes were nationalist, so no firm lean.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Corporatism subordinates individual economic interest to social function and the national interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The state requires every citizen to belong to an officially designated interest group, which implies group and state duties take precedence over individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No documented stance on environmental philosophy; the question lies outside what the doctrine addresses.

limit-population.rationale: Pronatalist family-centred regimes would oppose limits.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Order and continuity matter more than disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from reliance on human leaders and corporate bodies.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from surveillance and a police state.

restore-past-order.rationale: Catholic corporatists appeal to a medieval guild order, while Fascists claimed novelty; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Corporate states were built on a doctrine of organised functional bodies and common good, so adherents would not treat doctrine as secondary; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: The state controls political activity, and independent direct action is repressed.

means-match-ends.rationale: Regimes imposed corporate order from above through authoritarian means, which suggests adherents do not require means to mirror ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The sources never discuss foraging; rejection is inferred from a system that organises modern industries into sector bodies.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing the division of labour is never discussed; rejection is inferred from Quadragesimo Anno's bodies for each industry and profession (s2).

distribute-by-need.rationale: Implied: wages are set by function through employer and worker bodies, with Quadragesimo Anno asking only for a family-supporting wage.

production-for-use.rationale: Production stays for profit in private firms, subordinated to national goals.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno denies that the wage contract is unjust in itself and calls for capital and labour to cooperate, rejecting the exploitation thesis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Corporatism offers class collaboration as the alternative to Marxist class rule, and Quadragesimo Anno condemns communism's class warfare.

collective-farming.rationale: Implied: the rural population is described as committed to agrarianism within a private-property order; collective farming is not discussed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Corporatists reject Marxist claims and see capitalism reformable by organisation.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is central and taxation legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Implied by an authoritarian state whose political police persecuted opponents and which ordered society for national and moral ends.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Estado Novo was in theory a corporatist state representing interest groups rather than individuals, implying groups hold standing of their own.

conscription.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss conscription, but strong nationalist states of this type accepted it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Corporate statism requires membership in designated groups and offers neither voice via parties nor emphasis on exit; inferred from its compulsory-membership structure.

state-as-business.rationale: Implied: the state is the authority that compels membership in sector groups and mediates between them, not a service provider to customers who can leave.

positive-liberty.rationale: Welfare provisions imply some material support, but the concept is not used; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Regimes controlled media directly; the claim itself is not a doctrinal one.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Race science is not part of Salazarist or Catholic corporatism; Fascist Italy later adopted it.

organic-representation.rationale: The Estado Novo's Corporative Chamber seated municipalities and religious, cultural and professional groups as a state representing interest groups rather than individuals; representation through families comes from the Catholic model.

total-state.rationale: The Fascist formula is total statism, but other corporatist cases, such as Portugal, were more limited; the state was dominant in the economy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Regimes presented themselves as national regeneration after instability.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Italy expanded; Portugal sought only to hold its empire.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on a state, not feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Corporate states replaced guild and landlord ties with state-recognised workers' syndicates and wage contracts, not legal bondage to land.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not corporatist doctrine; inferred from an essentialist outlook.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic natural law underpins the Catholic strand.

single-common-good.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno wants each industry body to put the common interests of the whole trade first and the State to promote cooperation of the professions, which implies one common good over interest balancing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Corporate statism does not address Zionism, and its historical regimes held varied views; no basis for a lean.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; regimes' approaches to diaspora were a matter of national policy rather than corporatist principle.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a corporatist concern and the regimes did not share a policy on it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Representation is through state-recognised sectoral bodies, not worker votes in firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from regimes that placed education under state or Church direction rather than parental market choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Salazar was famed for balanced budgets; Italy was not so; contested.

economic-freedom.rationale: Free competition is distrusted, and political freedom was not tied to economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: These regimes relied on law, a political police and organised bodies as well as moral appeals, so adherents would not rest on example alone; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalist, yet colonial regimes denied it to others.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; sovereign nationalism supports unilateral action.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not a corporatist stance; the Catholic strand privileges faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Benefits were attached to national syndicate membership.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare was linked to employment through syndicates.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Corporatism article says the 1927 Labour Charter became the main form of class collaboration in the Fascist government, and Quadragesimo Anno urges cooperation in place of class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Regimes built on God, Fatherland and Family valued inherited institutions and tradition and would not sacrifice them to novelty.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed by corporatist doctrine; the regimes were nationalist and in places colonial, with no documented stance on anti-Western fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers are organised nationally under the state.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Estado Novo's family-centred ideology and its stricter voting rules for women reflect a distinct public role for the sexes.

ban-interest.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno does not call for a ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not Salazarist doctrine; Fascist Italy imposed it late; core view is no.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Corporate statism article describes the ruling party acting as a mediator between workers, capitalists and other major state interests, not as a class's tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; a state-directed national production outlook is inferred to favour domestic energy output.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist, culture-preserving regimes are inferred to expect assimilation; immigration was not a documented concern.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy theory outside corporatist doctrine; inferred rejection because corporate states did not frame politics this way.

proportional-representation.rationale: Corporate statism replaces party representation with representation through officially designated functional groups.

national-mission.rationale: Italy and Portugal had civilising mission rhetoric.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Estado Novo treated family and gender order as natural and would reject the claim that society systematically disadvantages women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Regimes attacked parliamentary politicians but stressed their own virtue.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Catholic regimes rejected eugenics generally; contested.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Estado Novo's secret police PIDE persecuted opponents and was shielded from accountability under the regime.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Estado Novo state exercised extensive authority over private investment decisions and the level of wages, far beyond defence, justice and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Portugal's lusotropicalism celebrated mixing in the empire, though Fascist Italy later enacted racial laws; mixed, inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Catholic belief in equal dignity but legal hierarchies by function and nation; split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Corporatism rejects socialism as such; Quadragesimo Anno says Christian socialism is a contradiction in terms.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Estado Novo treated overseas territories as extensions of Portugal and encouraged settlement, rejecting a colonial framing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine, and the regimes' relationship with religious law varied.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; the Catholic-aligned regimes privileged the Church but had no documented conversion law as part of corporatism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a concern of European corporate states; inferred rejection as it conflicts with their agrarian production interests.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the Estado Novo's grounding in Catholic social doctrine and its motto God, Fatherland and Family; the sources do not discuss religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine; corporate statists hold no stake, though a strong state is congenial to them.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority rests on the state, with plebiscites ritual.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionist, state-managed economies are inferred to prefer exporting more than importing.

population-transfer.rationale: Not documented as corporatist doctrine, and regimes varied.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Corporate states exercise state coercion and suppressed opposition, so adherents reject a rule against initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Free competition destroys itself; cooperation preferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Single-party regimes banned rivals; the Estado Novo allowed only the National Union party and tightly controlled opposition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican freedom concept foreign to corporate statism, which subordinates individuals to groups and the state; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Power was concentrated in the executive, as under Salazar, with a limited National Assembly.

vanguard-party.rationale: Corporatism rejects Marxist revolution and class politics; a revolutionary vanguard party is the opposite of class collaboration.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching stresses the poor but corporatism stresses function.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A policy of a late-twentieth-century democracy and not a corporatist question.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno describes the new syndical order as forbidding strikes and lock-outs, with the State intervening when the parties cannot settle a dispute.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno blames concentrations of economic power and failure of social order, not population; inferred rejection.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nationalist unity outlooks would favour the claim; inferred, not documented.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Corporate statism relies on appointed and group-designated authority, not random selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian corporate regimes tightly controlled opposition and ruled by emergency-style powers against enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state held broad authority over wages and prices in the corporate system.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposition was tightly controlled and press freedom limited in Estado Novo; direct party control is inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Armies in these regimes remained state institutions, often the regime's base, not party commands; no clear position.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nationalist regimes are inferred to restrict citizenship; no specific policy documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A populist-democratic demand foreign to hierarchical corporate states; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Single-party structures expected discipline, though the Estado Novo party was loosely run; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nationalist and sovereignty-focused regimes resisted supranational pooling.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The president or leader held executive control, with Salazar holding effective control of government in Portugal.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Catholic-aligned regimes supported the hierarchical Church; adherents of other confessions would differ, so low.

clerical-rule.rationale: Salazar rejected clerical rule even though Catholic.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Corporatism seeks national solidarity across classes and condemns the class war on which revolutionary defeatism depends.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Estado Novo's family-and-religion morality and control of opposition suggest support; the censorship regime is inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Estado Novo's presidents stood repeatedly and Salazar ruled for decades with no electoral check.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority flows from the top down; recalling officials by voters contradicts the anti-parliamentary design.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Portugal held NATO membership and the Anglo-Portuguese alliance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Private ownership continued under the corporatist mixed economy (s4), and nothing suggests banning rental housing; mild disagreement is inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Standing forces; Fascist militias were party arms.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Catholic and traditionalist regimes often idealised rural life; inferred and not central to corporatism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed by corporate statism as a doctrine.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the regimes drew on professional elites as well as populist rhetoric.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Regimes justified their empires by civilising claims such as lusotropicalism, implying hierarchy among societies.

death-penalty.rationale: Salazar abolished it; Italy reinstated; split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Catholic-traditional family morality opposes such curricula; inferred from the regimes' moral order.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed and the regimes' Catholic stance did not insist on creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Catholic-aligned and morality-based regimes restricted such material; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nationalist regimes are inferred to favour descent; not documented.

minority-language-support.rationale: Centralising national states are inferred to resist minority language support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Uniform state authority over groups suggests rejection; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Citizens are fitted into designated groups with considerable group control over members, leaving little room for eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Estado Novo was known for fiscal orthodoxy; cancellation of debts is inferred as rejected.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Colonial regimes did not support independence movements; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1933 constitution was imposed by a plebiscite engineered by Salazar, not drawn up by an elected assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: the Estado Novo was anti-parliamentary and held extensive authority over investment and wages, but its sources justify the restrictions by social order rather than as a temporary price of rapid growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nationalist priorities put national interest first; inferred, not documented.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Mixed; Portugal's president popularly elected nominally.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state held broad authority over investment and economic policy, so an independent bank is at odds with it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno says ownership has an individual and a social character, owners must consider the common good, and the State may define the duties of ownership.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Rejects communism; contested thesis not addressed.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine has no environmental stance.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed by corporatism; regimes' alliances varied.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Expansionist or colonial regimes would reject the claim in their own case; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Estado Novo was closely allied with the Catholic Church and drew on its social doctrine rather than curbing it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Split: Salazar held real power while a figurehead president existed, and a sovereign above parties fits some strands.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Estado Novo held its overseas territories as part of a single nation and fought to keep them; centralised states resist secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Centralised group-based organisation leaves little room for regional economic and legal autonomy; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Corporate states had leaders cults but not divine descent claims; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine's group organisation does not take a view on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Split: leaders held dominant authority but regimes issued constitutions and claimed legality.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed directly; functional representation resembles mixed rule in some readings but no documented stance.

leader-cult.rationale: Cult of leader was a feature in Italy; Salazar was less showy.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family ideology of the Estado Novo.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Corporatism rejects the premise of class struggle and of socialism itself.

land-redistribution.rationale: Landowners remained part of the corporate order; redistribution contradicts the mixed, private-ownership economy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Split: Fascist Italy pursued irredentist claims while the Estado Novo did not.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Catholic-aligned regimes did not criminalise leaving the faith; inferred rejection.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic regimes enforced modesty norms but not coverings by law.

common-currency.rationale: Nationalist and autarkic regimes preferred national control of money; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed by corporatism as such.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Centralised states recognise functional groups, not national minorities with their own institutions; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno rejects the Marxist account of history and a purely materialist view of society.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporate statism replaces market competition with government-directed sector bodies; Quadragesimo Anno attacks concentrated economic power but holds that free competition cannot direct economic life, so protecting competition is not the aim.

no-bailouts.rationale: Corporate states manage the economy actively and are inferred to support rescues; not documented.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; corporate states did not rely on majoritarian democracy or independent constitutional courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Traditional family and gender ideology opposes parity quotas; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Strong protectionism in the Estado Novo and autarky in Fascist Italy fit this, though it was not universal.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents split between protectionism and sovereignty.

moral-incentives.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno stresses duties and social charity but corporate regimes still used wages and profit.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Corporatism rejects revolutionary class politics, though Fascists themselves used armed squads; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hierarchy and social orders were preserved and not levelled by corporate states.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist education is inferred to centre the nation's own history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Estado Novo justified empire by lusotropicalism and civilising claims.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nation-centred regimes under God, Fatherland and Family used schools to inculcate loyalty; inferred from the motto.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed, though state direction of finance leans towards public control; no clear position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Corporatism claims that organised cooperation and reform can avoid collapse of capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: Fascist Italy sought Mediterranean and Roman-heritage influence and Portugal kept its empire, though not a defining doctrine of corporatism itself.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: both regimes pursued autarky and protectionism under state direction, though they did not seek to break all ties.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: corporatism denies class conflict and treats workers and employers as partners, so it rejects Marxist exploitation theory in either form.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: the state directs private dealings and compels sector membership, so unfettered private choice is not a value, though the regimes tolerated discrimination in their own ways.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Authoritarian state-corporatist regimes rejected liberal constitutional limits and gave the state primacy over individual rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Portugal and Italy held colonial empires as national missions and defended their borders, so imposed treaties are not set aside.

elective-rulers.rationale: Authoritarian regimes replaced competitive elections with state-controlled selection; Portugal had a president chosen with a dominant prime minister; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: The corporative state makes the common good, as defined by the state, binding on all groups, leaving no individual veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Authoritarian corporatism holds the ruler answerable to the nation, not to subjects' right of removal; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Estado Novo and Fascist Italy were anti-parliamentarist and replaced party-based parliaments with corporative chambers.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Catholic traditionalist corporatists generally taught kindness to animals; inferred, not a stated issue in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Use of animals is accepted in Catholic and traditionalist outlooks, with kindness expected; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno holds that owners must use surplus wealth for the common good and charity, and class collaboration rests on mutual duties.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Estado Novo encouraged depoliticisation of ordinary citizens, while Italy mobilised them; adherents lean against private withdrawal, which is inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The regimes used press and mass organisations as tools of mobilisation, and adherents would not accept this critique; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The regimes built consent through state-sponsored corporative bodies and propaganda, not only force; inferred from the corporatist system.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Fascist Italy used 'proletarian nation' claims against richer powers, but Portugal did not; adherents are split.

native-born-offices.rationale: The nationalist regimes favoured citizens of the nation for public office; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Nationalist regimes stress sovereign independence from foreign directing centres; inferred, since communist parties are not the issue.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Fascist Italy pursued autarky and Estado Novo ran a protectionist economy aimed at national self-sufficiency.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Fascist Italy pursued irredentist claims, while Portugal did not; inferred for the family as a whole.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Portuguese colonial rule kept political power with the metropolitan state over native populations; inferred from the empire.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The corporative regimes were founded in opposition to liberalism, socialism and antifascism, and banned antifascist parties.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents condemn communism but defended their own regimes, and Salazar rejected the totalitarian label for the Estado Novo.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War was not an issue for the corporatist regimes; adherents have no stake in it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Nationalist traditionalist regimes valued national heritage monuments; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The regimes' Catholic-traditionalist family model did not treat men as a disadvantaged group; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The traditional family model gave no equal-service case for male victims; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The regimes explicitly rejected liberal democracy in favour of corporative forms they thought suited their nations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Estado Novo arose from the 1926 military coup and the army remained its pillar; Fascist Italy also treated the armed forces as guardians of the state.

paid-care-work.rationale: The regimes' family policy was pronatalist and expected women to care at home, without wages; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: The Catholic-traditionalist regimes and Quadragesimo Anno stress family duty; inferred from their social teaching.

office-by-exam.rationale: Corporatist regimes favoured appointed and competitive technocratic selection over party elections; inferred, with low confidence.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Italy and Portugal pursued economic nationalism and state direction of key industries; inferred from that.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Fascist Italy had no divorce and the Estado Novo restricted it for Catholic marriages, so adherents oppose easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The state recognises and controls representation by sector and replaces party competition; binding and recalling delegates runs against that.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The regimes ran state-supervised social insurance through the corporative bodies, not private accounts; inferred from that.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property survived under state direction; no regime made land tenure depend on use. Inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Corporatist states subordinated parliament to the executive and the corporative chambers; budget control by an elected parliament was weakened.

single-official-language.rationale: Italy and Portugal promoted a national language and culture; inferred, low confidence, as Portugal was already largely monolingual.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalist and autarkic regimes favoured keeping land in citizen hands; inferred, with low confidence.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Authoritarian-corporatist regimes rejected equality-based rights claims and group-outcome tests; inferred from that.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Catholic social teaching in Quadragesimo Anno criticises materialism and consumerism; inferred, with low confidence.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Italy backed foreign movements for its aims while Portugal stayed cautious; adherents split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Italy and Portugal backed authoritarian allies in the Spanish Civil War, so a great power policing its bloc is inferred as acceptable.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the state's role as arbiter above sectoral interests and from the rejection of liberal parliament and lobbying politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, authoritarian character of the regimes, which tightly controlled civil society and the press.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fascist Italy ran a pro-natal campaign and Catholic traditionalist Portugal favoured the family; inferred, not set out in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the strong centralised state, which leaves little room for local authorities to restrict property sales.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Fascist Labour Charter treated work as a social duty and the state directed employment and wages; a guarantee is inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the regimes rejected liberal democracy and parliaments, so they would not see spreading democracy as the route to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The authoritarian state demands obedience, and the Estado Novo constitution placed the state above individuals and parties.

non-intervention.rationale: Fascist Italy pursued interventionist wars while Salazar's Portugal stayed neutral, so adherents were split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Compulsory syndicates were organised by economic sector, with workers and employers together in each branch.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred; Fascist Italy turned antisemitic late and Portugal did not, so conspiracy claims were not a common feature of the strand.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno and the Estado Novo defended marriage and the family as basic institutions under church and state.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Estado Novo ran censorship and a political police, so state secrecy was the norm.

local-production.rationale: The Estado Novo was protectionist and aimed at economic self-sufficiency; inferred for the strand as a whole.

informal-organisation.rationale: The system required officially recognised formal bodies for every sector and banned independent organising.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, sovereignty-first character of these regimes, which put national decisions above outside bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-traditionalist character of the Estado Novo and Quadragesimo Anno, though Fascist Italy was less tied to religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist and imperial outlook of the regimes, which sought primacy rather than formal equality or ritual submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: a centralised, unitary authoritarian state leaves regions no claim to retain revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Private property in the means of production survives, defended by Quadragesimo Anno and the regimes.

defeat-communism.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno condemns socialism and the Estado Novo and Fascist Italy were anti-communist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from subsidiarity and recognised vocational bodies delivering social functions under state supervision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Catholic-traditionalist regimes upheld religion as true and socially necessary.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno criticises liberal free competition and capital concentration, and corporatism is offered as the alternative.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-traditionalist, family-centred character of the regimes.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: the Estado Novo's family motto and Catholic subsidiarity place care in the family.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from nationalist cultural policy; Fascist Italy campaigned against foreign words, though this was not central to the doctrine.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: an authoritarian state keeps treaty and sovereign prerogative and is unlikely to be bound against its own judgement.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Corporate statism puts groups under state control rather than self-governing communities holding common property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from imperial settlement policy in the Portuguese and Italian empires.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Corporatism was presented as a third path between liberal capitalism and socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The nationalist regimes used appeals to history and heritage; inferred, as the doctrine is economic and institutional.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The doctrine does not deny the Holocaust, and Portugal stayed outside the war; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Catholic-traditionalist regimes upheld moral order through law; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Corporate statism replaces party competition and class conflict with state-controlled groups within an authoritarian state.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Catholic-traditionalist regimes protected the religious order; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Italy and Portugal held overseas empires and governed them in the interest of the metropole.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that Catholic-nationalist regimes would not endorse an Islamic doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Corporate statism upholds order and existing authority rather than removal of rulers by force; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Decisions go through state-recognised functional groups under an authoritarian state, not direct popular participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine rejects class conflict as a frame and unites classes under the nation and state; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; the Catholic-traditionalist regimes would reject it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic teaching, which the regimes drew on, opposes it; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Corporate statism presents itself as a third way beyond left and right and class conflict; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: The doctrine holds that employers and workers cooperate under state arbitration, and does not see labour as alienated by capital; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Catholic-nationalist outlook of the regimes.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Salazar's regime and Catholic social teaching ground authority in God's order, though Fascist Italy differed; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Catholic-traditionalist character of the regimes.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; the state-directed system limited workers' rights to independent action; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The doctrine keeps private ownership and mixes it with state direction and Catholic-inspired social protection, a third way between laissez-faire and full state control; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: These are authoritarian, nationalist regimes that built and valued strong armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: State direction of investment and wages aims at national development under state control, not letting some get rich first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Portugal stayed neutral in WWII while Fascist Italy joined the Axis, so the strands split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession was not a regime principle in Italy or Portugal; inferred from their leader-and-party structures.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Corporate states kept private banking under state direction, and Quadragesimo Anno criticised finance power but did not call for user-owned banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The regimes favoured national self-sufficiency but Salazar also stressed balanced budgets; no clear position.

property-franchise.rationale: Fascist Italy and Estado Novo restricted the franchise by property, literacy, or syndicate membership; inferred from that practice.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The regimes' traditionalist, patriarchal family ideology makes this thesis inferred to be strongly rejected.

reification.rationale: The corporatist view is that class cooperation, not class domination, governs the economy; Marxist concepts are inferred to be rejected.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Corporatist doctrine denies class conflict, and the state controlled the press; inferred rejection.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Both regimes ruled largely by decree-laws and a strong executive, so the rule-of-standing-law ideal is inferred to be weak.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial franchises were not core corporatist doctrine, but Portugal limited rights for colonial natives; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from anti-parliamentarism and state-controlled participation through syndicates.

open-government-data.rationale: The regimes practiced censorship and secrecy, so open records are inferred to be strongly rejected.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Catholic-traditionalist character of Estado Novo and the Italian Concordat support religious marriage rules; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Italy's 1938 racial laws were state-run and not consumer boycotts; inferred mild disagreement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Corporatism replaces popular and party politics with state-recognised functional bodies and an authoritarian state, so decision by lay citizens chosen by lot runs against its core design.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The regimes leaned on Catholic traditionalism and Quadragesimo Anno's fixed social teaching; reinterpretation for modern conditions is inferred as unwelcome.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno condemns the concentration of economic power in a few hands as a despotic dictatorship, and corporatism aimed to subordinate capital to the state; its remedy is state direction, not liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-traditionalist and nationalist character of the Italian, Portuguese and Austrian regimes; the sources do not discuss military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The regimes were Catholic-aligned (Lateran accords, Estado Novo's Church ties) and none promoted atheism through schools.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A strong authoritarian state with a powerful police apparatus is central to the model, so abolition is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Corporatism shares influence among functional sectors, not among rival communities, and rule stays with one leader; inferred from that structure.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Catholic social teaching praises charity and intermediate bodies, but corporate statism has the state organise and direct welfare through its syndicates; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Leaders such as Mussolini and Salazar ruled without term limits and the model replaces electoral competition; inferred, not directly discussed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Representation runs through state-recognised functional bodies rather than individual vote delegation; inferred from the corporatist structure.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The question did not arise for interwar corporatists and nothing in the sources fixes an answer.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist Catholic orientation of these regimes, in which clerical offices are male.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist family law of Estado Novo and Fascist Italy that kept the husband as head of the family.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a state that restricts political participation and ties representation to recognised functional groups of citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state direction of wages and prices, which would include housing, though ownership stays private.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Catholic and Spannian respect for property and hierarchy, which treats creators' rights as legitimate.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Fascist Italy and the Estado Novo ran state youth organisations (Balilla, Mocidade Portuguesa) to train youth for the nation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from regimes that valued military strength and national power.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; sources are silent and regimes differed, as Portugal hosted allied facilities while Italy pursued independent power.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from authoritarian, nationalist regimes that avoided self-incrimination and official admission of state crimes.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno favours a just wage for work and criticises pure capital power, while keeping private property; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Catholic teaching and the regimes accepted lethal force for defence of person and state.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from nationalist myth-making, such as Fascist appeals to ancient Rome, though Portugal's differed.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regimes' Catholic-traditionalist view of fixed sex roles.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regimes' traditionalist view of woman's place in family and nation.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Fascist cult of the fallen, though Portugal's regime was more restrained.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from Catholic-traditionalist framing of social order as moral and religious, but not stated as doctrine.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from a state-centred nationalism that wanted all of its people within its territory.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the strong state being the first and central instrument of national order.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic-traditionalist keeping of established liturgical language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic teaching treating tradition and scripture as authoritative as they stand.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nationalist regimes favouring the national group in economic life, though corporatism itself is sectoral.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; irredentism varied among the regimes and is not a feature of the corporatist system itself.

independent-unions.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno describes the Italian corporative system as replacing free unions with state-recognised syndicates, and Estado Novo likewise bound unions to the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Corporate statism rejects class struggle and working-class rule in favour of state arbitration among sectors.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Regimes varied between state and private provision of local services; inferred, with no doctrinal position.

second-chamber.rationale: Corporate systems typically replaced or complemented elected chambers with a chamber of corporations, as in Portugal's Corporative Chamber and Fascist Italy's Chamber of Fasces and Corporations.

municipal-property.rationale: Private ownership survives under state direction, and the state, not the locality, sits at the centre; local collective ownership is not part of the system.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The system is a top-down authoritarian state, so decisions rest with the state, not local assemblies coordinated by delegates.

family-wage.rationale: Catholic social teaching in Quadragesimo Anno holds that wages should be enough to support a worker and his family, and Estado Novo promoted the male-breadwinner household.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred to be indifferent, since state direction could point either way.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; state direction of research could support it but nothing in the doctrine says so.

anonymous-payments.rationale: An authoritarian state that directs investment, wages and prices would not allow untraceable money; inferred from its control of the economy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the authoritarian regimes' censorship and secret police, which could not tolerate anonymous speech.

person-over-state.rationale: Corporate statism subordinates individuals to the state and the functional groups; Quadragesimo Anno stresses human dignity but the regimes treated the person as serving the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno and the Catholic-traditionalist regimes, notably Salazar's, held that society should serve spiritual as well as material ends.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Authoritarian unitary states held all regional and local power at the centre's discretion, as in Salazar's centralised Portugal.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; inferred to be indifferent, as state-directed agriculture pursued productivity.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; the regimes pursued both urban and ruralist policies, and Estado Novo idealised the countryside.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Catholic corporatism and Salazar's Portugal rejected racial politics, while Fascist Italy only later adopted racial laws; inferred as a rejection because the system organises by sector, not race.

racial-pride.rationale: Regimes differed: Italy later promoted racial doctrine and Portugal emphasised imperial and Catholic pride; inferred, with adherents split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Fascist Italy waged wars of conquest in Ethiopia and elsewhere while Portugal fought only to keep its colonies; inferred as a disagreement, though regimes varied.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Fascist Italy used linguistic irredentism while Salazar's Portugal and Austria's Federal State did not; the strands split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Corporatist representation was by economic function and under single-party control, not by religious community; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The regimes were strongly nationalist and cultivated a sense of foreign encirclement; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Education was shaped by the regime's ideology and social hierarchy, not offered as a universal free entitlement; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; the regimes preferred state direction of industry to market-based levies, so inferred disagreement.

future-generations.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the traditionalist, nation-as-continuing-organism outlook of these regimes.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Catholic-traditionalist regimes assigned women a domestic role and gave them little public voice; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Italy was openly militarist and the regimes prized strong state power; inferred disagreement.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Authoritarian regimes conducted foreign policy by executive discretion and secrecy; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The state directed investment and the economy, and Italy and Portugal ran autarkic policies with controls on capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Strong authoritarian corporatist states claimed a monopoly of force, disbanding rival armed groups or absorbing them into the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Fascist Italy and the Estado Novo demanded discipline and obedience from soldiers; refusal would be treason.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wages were set through state-sanctioned corporations or compulsory arbitration, not free bargaining by independent unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The regimes had state-run welfare and family allowances but no documented tax-credit tradition; adherents are split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Corporate statism favours strong state direction of the economy, not legal limits on the state; Salazar's balanced budgets were a policy, not a binding rule. Inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Fascist Italy sought autarky and revision of the international order in its own favour; the developing-country framing is anachronistic and inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Corporate statism builds on and strengthens the existing state by incorporating organised groups into it (s1); smashing the state is not discussed directly.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The system imposes a state-defined blueprint of sectoral corporations rather than letting communities choose economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the interwar regimes; their conservation was state-directed rather than market-valued. Inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The regimes and their Catholic-traditionalist and nationalist outlook treated the nation as an organic community above individuals.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No documented position; inferred from state direction and conservative fiscal practice.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The regimes stressed national unity and organic harmony, rejecting class or regional exploitation framings; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Catholic social teaching, a source of corporatism, grounds dignity in a fixed human nature; Fascist Italy's view differed.

public-service-media.rationale: The regimes controlled the press and broadcasting for state purposes, not independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-traditionalist regimes, which held one revealed religion true; not a doctrinal point of corporatism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Corporatism organises each economic sector, agriculture included, into state-recognised bodies that coordinate prices and production, so state support for farmers fits.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the strong nationalist state and its priority on national power; the issue is not addressed in the sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: Corporate statism replaces class conflict and party competition with officially designated sectoral bodies, leaving no place for an independent workers' party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred; the regimes' penal codes were modern and authoritarian, but the practice is not discussed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-traditionalist and patriarchal character of Italy and Portugal, whose laws kept male privileges in family and property.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The sources do not address language classification; inferred indifference.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The state directs the economy through sectoral bodies and arbitration, so ex ante state control rather than private suits fits the model.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Corporatist chambers represent economic sectors, not traditional rulers; inferred that custom-based bodies have no formal place.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the subordination of individual interests to the state's direction; environment as such is not discussed.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian emphasis on order and state power in the Italian and Portuguese regimes.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist regimes' emphasis on national unity and culture; not a documented requirement.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Syndicates were state-recognised and membership dues were levied on all workers in the sector, so union membership was effectively compulsory.

voter-id.rationale: Not a corporatist concern; the regimes controlled who could vote and electoral roll rules were secondary. Inferred as split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Catholic traditionalist regimes (Italy after the Lateran Pacts, Estado Novo, Austria) gave the Catholic Church a privileged legal position.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: It replaces party competition with state-arbitrated cooperation among functional groups, so competitive elections do not define legitimate government.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the regimes' Catholic-traditionalist social morality, which condemned sex outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the strong authoritarian state's readiness to curb communications to preserve order.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: welfare ran through state-controlled syndicates and social insurance, not an unconditional cash transfer.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: Italy and Portugal restricted women's vote, and Catholic corporatism stressed the family as the unit of representation.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from Catholic traditionalism, which treated religion as support for the family order rather than a source of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Adherents split: Fascist Italy adopted racial laws in 1938 while Portugal and Austria did not make race central.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: the regimes promoted a patriarchal family model and had no state agencies for gender equality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The doctrine puts property under state-directed national interest, so an unconditional first-claim title is unlikely; inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Regimes stressed national sovereignty and resisted external courts; the question is anachronistic, so inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Catholic corporatists and secular Fascists differed on the place of scripture; adherents are split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The regimes were patriarchal and presented family and gender roles as part of the order; inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Private ownership survived under state direction, and these regimes were anti-socialist, so defending a nationalised planned state is not expected; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Corporatist systems built higher chambers from delegates of the occupational bodies rather than direct popular votes.

national-church-status.rationale: The Estado Novo and the Austrian state were Catholic-corporatist and gave the Church a privileged place, following Quadragesimo Anno.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Authoritarian nationalist regimes favoured unitary national states over minority autonomy; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the strong unitary state and nationalism; popular votes on territory did not feature.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic; Salazar's regime held its own colonies and had no doctrine on postcolonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by corporatist theory; Catholic frugality and state development goals pull in different directions.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the nationalism and state control of these regimes.

equal-conscription.rationale: Regimes with patriarchal, militarised ideals did not treat the sexes equally in service; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, blood-and-soil rhetoric of Fascist Italy and the Estado Novo; the doctrine itself is about economic organisation.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the regimes used political repression, but drug dealing was not a doctrinal issue and the Catholic-legalist regimes kept formal courts.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the anti-communist, Western and Catholic orientation of the interwar corporatist regimes; China was not a concern.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Fascist Italian irredentism and nationalism toward Italians abroad; not part of corporatist doctrine itself.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: corporatism keeps private property under state direction and Quadragesimo Anno defends property, with no equal-ownership or compensation doctrine.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the organic, state-first view in which individuals and their labour are integrated into state-recognised groups and the national interest.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine says nothing on consumption taxes, and regimes financed themselves variously.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: social insurance was run through syndicates for members, neither universal nor means-tested for the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Parties were abolished or subordinated, but interest groups were deliberately incorporated as state-recognised bodies, so adherents agree on one half and not the other.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: the state granted licences and cartels to favoured firms, but adherents also stressed subordinating business to national interest, so no clear stance.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: Portugal and Austria were Catholic-aligned while Fascist Italy was less so, and the doctrine's groups are by sector, not denomination.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from the regimes' pairing of modernising state-led industry with traditionalist Catholic and national values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-traditionalist family policy of the Estado Novo and Italy; divorce was restricted and not a doctrinal topic.

national-resource-control.rationale: Italy and Portugal pursued protectionist, state-directed economies with national control of key sectors and colonial resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Corporatist regimes set wages, prices and investment by the common good and treated property as socially bound, so fairness was judged by outcome and function; inferred from Quadragesimo Anno and the state-directed economy.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: State direction of finance and condemnation of unchecked financial power in Catholic social teaching suggest support for curbing speculation; inferred, not documented.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Neither regime treated racism as a main obstacle for domestic groups; inferred from their nationalist, class-collaborationist framing.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Catholic-corporatist adherents lean on natural law while the Fascist state treated law as the state's will, so adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno stresses the dignity and value of work and vocational groups of employed workers; inferred opposition to replacing paid work.

multipolar-world.rationale: Authoritarian nationalist regimes sought their own spheres and empire (Portugal, Italy) against liberal and Soviet powers; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno holds that capital and labour need each other in production, rejecting labour as the sole source of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The corporate state binds class collaboration to national unity, presenting service to the nation as service to its producers.

material-over-identity.rationale: Corporatism subordinates class interest to national unity and the Catholic-nationalist order, so identity and nation outrank a materialist left agenda; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Private ownership under an authoritarian state is accepted, but Quadragesimo Anno rejects socialism and communist leadership; the statement's socialist framing is rejected.

missingStatements.text: Strikes and lock-outs should be forbidden, with disputes between employers and workers settled by a public authority.
missingStatements.rationale: Quadragesimo Anno describes the Italian corporative system as forbidding strikes and lock-outs and sending unresolved disputes to state arbitration, and the Fascist system made the state final arbiter.

missingStatements.text: Every worker and employer should be required to belong to one officially recognised body for their sector.
missingStatements.rationale: Corporate statism requires citizens to belong to officially designated interest groups, usually by economic sector.

notes: Fascist Italy, Salazar's Portugal and Catholic corporatists differ: Italy was more totalitarian, militarist and expansionist, Portugal more conservative and Church-aligned, and Quadragesimo Anno voices reservations about state-run syndicates. Many answers on social and foreign policy are low-confidence inferences.
